races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Colliers Quay
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for Eoin Christopher McCarthy's yard, which posts 1/9 in the 14-day window; only one run in similar going showed a finishing position of fifth from 18 — needs to find improvement but a prominent style suits this steady tempo.

runners_data.name: Coolishael
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, though tagged as racing out of role as a lead type, which is a genuine concern; has placed twice in similar good going but the 79-day layoff and the out-of-role flag temper confidence despite its commanding tactical position.

runners_data.name: Discrete
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse redistributed into a midfield slot that will feel unnatural; recent form strings of 7-7-13 in similar going are discouraging and its style does not align well with the likely slow pace, regardless of its mapped position.

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator shown in midfield purely because the rear is over-subscribed; carries a fades-in-finish flag and a form string of P-P00 in good ground, making it difficult to construct a winning scenario even if it does find clear ground late.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Prominent-style seven-year-old who has the potential to slot into an ideal handy position off the sole front-runner; trainer Thomas Gibney takes 0/3 in 14 days but this horse's style fits the expected race shape better than most at these weights.

runners_data.name: Noharmintrying
runners_data.note: Completely unraced with unknown style and going preference; trainer Aidan Anthony Howard is 2/3 in the 14-day window which is an eye-catching stat, and a fresh debut type could be well-schooled enough to exploit a modest gallop if it has the ability.

runners_data.name: Nothintodowithme
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fades-in-finish flag who has managed only a P and an 8 in two runs on similar going; a slow pace does not help a horse that already struggles to sustain its effort in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish and was ninth in similar good going on its most recent outing; hold-up style is a natural fit for a strong-run race that this race shape is unlikely to produce, limiting its prospects.

runners_data.name: Tommy Go Maith
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with four P finishes in its form string and a fades-in-finish concern; the redistribution into midfield will not rescue it given it already cannot sustain its run from the back, and the good ground record shows three finishes without a win or a place.

runners_data.name: Vargas
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner has strong institutional support with the trainer posting 4/37 in 14 days; one run at 5th in similar going is modest but hold-up style means it needs the race to develop in its favour — a sustainable pace from Coolishael could suit if it can track the pace from the midfield zone.

runners_data.name: Green Grass
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with form of 00 and a fades-in-finish flag, with both runs in good going ending in 12th and 13th; pushed into midfield because the rear is over-subscribed, but in truth a weak profile regardless of where it lines up tactically.

runners_data.name: Myhero La Colmine
runners_data.note: Unraced four-year-old with unknown style and going preference for Paul John Gilligan's yard which is 0/9 in 14 days — no form angle to attack and a quiet trainer run rate makes this a very speculative entry.

runners_data.name: Elusive Truce
runners_data.note: Lightly raced six-year-old for Charlie Keegan who has no 14-day runners on record; with unknown style and going preference this is a difficult horse to assess and carries maximum pace-map uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a fades-in-finish flag and form figures of P00 in good going; shuffled into the midfield map because hold-up slots are over-subscribed, but its actual running position will be further back in a race where a slow tempo will leave it with nothing to run onto.

runners_data.name: Roll It Roisin
runners_data.note: Hold-up style from David Harry Kelly's yard, which posts 1/9 in 14 days; one run in similar going produced seventh from a starting position and a tongue-tie is noted, but with a steady pace the hold-up profile is not well served.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Unknown style with form of 6-7-6 across similar and soft ground; the consistent mid-field finishes suggest a horse that does not accelerate off a slow pace and the trainer's 14-day record of 0/4 adds no confidence.

runners_data.name: Beyond Forgiveness
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for David Harry Kelly with a single run showing 6th in similar going; unknown style makes it hard to assess but the one data point from good ground is not encouraging.

runners_data.name: Don't Tell Paddy
runners_data.note: Unraced four-year-old for Eoin Christopher McCarthy, whose yard posts 1/9 in 14 days; no style or going data available and debut runners in 18-horse maiden hurdles face a significant challenge without known form lines.

races.paceDynamic: Coolishael is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner maiden hurdle and, critically, is tagged as racing out of role at the head of affairs — meaning even the one horse expected to lead may not do so with full conviction or natural comfort. With no other confirmed front-runner pressing for the lead, the early pace is likely to be steady and uncontested, creating a single-file procession on good ground at Ballinrobe over 2m2½f. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Leva Deva, Lastofthenatives, Green Grass, and Discrete are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield positions they will not naturally find, meaning the race shape behind Coolishael is likely to be bunched and traffic-prone. A controlled tempo with one horse controlling from the front on decent ground will suit horses that can travel prominently or in a handy position off a slow pace, rather than those relying on a strong gallop to deliver a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coolishael Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Coolishael leads without serious pressure and dictates a steady, sustainable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Coolishael sets the fractions from the front on good ground, and without any rival applying early pressure the race turns into a test of jumping and staying power from the head of affairs; horses able to travel prominently just off the pace are ideally positioned to pounce at the second-last. Prominent-style horses like Minella Post and Colliers Quay, who can race handily without fighting for position, benefit most from a soft early gallop that rewards fluency and a well-timed challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough that a horse tracking the leader in third or fourth position coasts into contention and wins going away.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field and allows a horse sitting just off the pace to avoid any jumping errors from the front while saving enough for the run-in; on good ground over this trip the winner is often a horse that jumps the last two hurdles fluently from a prominent position. Vargas, trained by Gordon Elliott and carrying strong market expectation, and Colliers Quay both profile as horses who could slot into this prime midfield-to-prominent position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If traffic issues among the redistributed midfield pack create a split that allows a genuine hold-up horse to weave through.
scenarios.body: The overcrowded midfield — stuffed with true hold-up horses such as Leva Deva, Lastofthenatives, and Green Grass pushed out of their natural rear position — creates a chaotic mid-race order, and if any one of them can find a clear passage on the run to two out a late run becomes possible. This scenario is materially discounted because these horses are not true midfield racers and are likely to be disadvantaged by the traffic and the slow early pace that will have already done its damage by the time gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Debutant Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced or lightly raced unknown-style runners — Noharmintrying, Myhero La Colmine, Elusive Truce, or Don't Tell Paddy — is vastly superior on debut.
scenarios.body: A well-prepared unknown quantity from a yard with live form could exploit a modest pace by travelling in the right position without the baggage of established form lines; on good ground in a weak maiden the bar is not high. This is low probability because none of these horses have a known running style that fits a definable scenario and the tactical uncertainty is very high.

watchPoints.text: Coolishael is the only confirmed front-runner but is tagged as racing out of role — watch whether it actually shows up at the head of affairs at the start, because if it drops away from the lead the pace collapses entirely and the race becomes a sprint from the last.

The midfield is dangerously overcrowded with redistributed hold-up types (Leva Deva, Lastofthenatives, Green Grass, Discrete) — watch for a traffic pile-up or interference between the third-last and second-last hurdle as these horses try to find gaps that do not exist.

Noharmintrying's trainer Aidan Anthony Howard is 2/3 in the 14-day window — watch market moves on this debutant, as a well-backed newcomer from a yard in form could be carrying significant stable confidence regardless of the pace map uncertainty.

Vargas for Gordon Elliott is the highest-profile hold-up type in the field — watch whether Josh Williamson tries to push up from the midfield slot rather than sitting deep, as a pace-change decision early could significantly alter how much of a run this horse gets.

Minella Post is the only prominent-style horse apart from Coolishael that has consistent good-ground runs on the board — watch its jumping, as a horse that travels fluently in second or third off the lone front-runner is best placed to win this race if Coolishael's lead is not extreme.

races.name: Hollymount Nursing Home Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Manoir De Mirande
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two consecutive wins over 18f on Good for Gordon Elliott; holds the front-running role by default in this field and carries 166lbs but the 7lb claimer Joshua Halford compensates; Good ground suits (7/11 sim-going record includes 2 wins), and 18 days since last run is a routine refresh rather than a concern.
runners_data.comment: Manoir De Mirande arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, with a runner-up finish last time out keeping him in the form of his life, and he has experience of today's trip and going; 18 days between runs is a perfectly acceptable gap for the top-rated contender here.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: Won last two starts over 18-19f on Good for Andrew Slattery, showing a sharp upturn in form; natural hold-up runner who needs things to happen in front of him, and with so many rivals wanting to come from off the pace the finish-line traffic could be a factor; the ⚠ fade flag is worth noting given the crowded rear.
runners_data.comment: O'Grady Cracker arrives in red-hot form, winning back-to-back last time out and two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; the main concern is that his 163 lb burden could blunt that momentum.

runners_data.name: Houndsworth
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose best effort came when winning over 16f on Good; McNiff's yard is cold (0 from 9 in 14 days) and recent form reads 654, suggesting a flat patch; 7lb claim for Alan King is a small positive, and 14 days since last run is fine, but the horse needs significant improvement on latest figures.
runners_data.comment: Houndsworth has run over today's trip and going, arrives fit on a 14-day turnaround, and our rating of 111 marks him out as a serious threat; the concern is that he has not won in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been running consistently below expectations (7R560) with zero wins from 15 runs on similar going; only five days since last run raises a mild freshness query, and Paul Flynn's yard has been modestly active (1/23 T14); occupies a role as pace companion to the leader but offers limited winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn from a yard striking at just 4% in the last fortnight, William F Browne faces an uphill task, though he has experience of today's going and ran just five days ago.

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Two recent wins over 20f on Good mark him as a progressive stayer, and Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking; his natural style is true hold-up, yet the overcrowded rear means he has been mapped to midfield — a position that neither plays to his strengths nor guarantees a clear passage when he needs it most.
runners_data.comment: Ocean Murphy finished second last time out, which maintains his recent profile, but his win two starts back is sandwiched by some poor efforts and he ranks fifth of six on our figures, making him hard to fancy at this level despite a prompt return and going experience.

runners_data.name: Nile Star
runners_data.note: Returning after 43 days and yet to win at the current track trip-distance combination (0W0P on sim-going); the ⚠ fade flag compounds concerns, and being a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of closers in the field further reduces his chance of landing a telling blow at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Nile Star faces a stiff task here; experience on today's going is a minor plus, but 141 lb is a significant burden for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Manoir De Mirande is the sole confirmed front runner in a field of six and, with no rival likely to push for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Ballinrobe's tight circuit over 2m2½f on Good ground. William F Browne is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and may track Manoir De Mirande, but he brings a poor recent record and is unlikely to apply meaningful pressure. The hold-up contingent — O'Grady Cracker, Houndsworth, Ocean Murphy and Nile Star — is oversized relative to the pace on offer, meaning the rear of the field will be congested and closers will need to navigate traffic before they can challenge. This race shape strongly favours Manoir De Mirande and any horse capable of racing prominently in an uncontested lead scenario, as a single front runner setting a measured tempo on Good ground is the classic recipe for a front-runner's day; true hold-up horses face extra risk because the field holds more hold-up types than genuine back-markers, and Ocean Murphy and Nile Star — both redistributed to midfield from their natural rear position — are least likely to secure the ground they need to finish best.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Manoir De Mirande Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Manoir De Mirande secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a steady, rhythm-friendly gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Manoir De Mirande, in excellent recent form (two wins from last three over 18f on Good), bowls along in front and uses the Ballinrobe track to his advantage, never coming off the bridle until he presses the button; the prominent runners behind him lack the firepower to close the gap when he extends.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pegs Back
scenarios.trigger: If William F Browne or another prominent type tracks Manoir De Mirande closely enough to apply pressure in the straight and force a battle.
scenarios.body: A contested front-end duel depletes Manoir De Mirande's reserves late, cracking open the race for a horse able to travel prominently without expending early energy; O'Grady Cracker, coming off back-to-back wins, would be best placed to sweep past a tiring leader from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and Manoir De Mirande ties up in the final flight, leaving the race to a horse produced with a late run.
scenarios.body: Ocean Murphy arrives on the back of two wins over 20f on Good and has the stamina profile to finish powerfully; however, both Ocean Murphy and Nile Star are redistributed from true hold-up positions and may not secure the clear run needed, making this scenario fragile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Claims Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race unravels through jumping errors or fallers, reducing the field and handing an opportunity to a lesser-fancied runner.
scenarios.body: Houndsworth won over 16f on Good and carries a 7lb claim for Alan King, giving a lightly weighted profile that could benefit from chaos; Nile Star has shown a recurring tendency to fade and is the least likely beneficiary here.

watchPoints.text: Manoir De Mirande's lead must be monitored at the top of the home straight — if he quickens smoothly there without challenge, the race is effectively over; any sign of a jumping error or a shortening stride is the only trigger for the scenarios behind him.

O'Grady Cracker and Houndsworth will likely be jostling for position in a congested hold-up group; watch for crowding on the final bend as multiple closers attempt to fan wide simultaneously, which could cost ground at a crucial moment.

Ocean Murphy's jockey Darragh O'Keeffe may be forced to commit earlier than ideal given the midfield mapping; if O'Keeffe can't find a clear run between the last two hurdles, his powerful finishing style is negated.

William F Browne's five-day turnaround is unusually quick for a horse with a 7R560 recent sequence — watch how he travels in the first half mile; if he is struggling to keep tabs on Manoir De Mirande before halfway, he becomes irrelevant.

Nile Star's 43-day absence and habitual late fade make him the most likely horse to drop away under pressure on the run-in; jockey Shane Markey (7) will need to produce a tactically precise ride to extract any value.

races.name: Paddy Smyth Memorial Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's prominent racer has a strong record on Good ground (4 from 4 sim-going samples, one win, two places) and comes into this off 38 days, which is a manageable gap; Jordan Gainford takes the ride and the 2m6½f trip looks well within reach based on recent runs at 18f.|

runners_data.name: Amina
runners_data.note: John McConnell's six-year-old has four placed efforts on Good ground from five attempts and clearly handles the surface well; the 71-day absence is worth noting but the tongue-tie, consistent form figure, and step back to Good from softer looks a positive switch.|

runners_data.name: Clash Gold
runners_data.note: Ran a clear personal best when second last time at Gowran on Good, but that effort came from a genuine hold-up position this horse prefers — with the map placing it in midfield due to redistribution, it may not get the late-run scenario its style demands, tempering its claims despite that eye-catching recent effort.|

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott's yard gives this prominent-style mare strong market credentials; she has placed twice on Good ground and the 2m6½f trip looks a natural extension from her recent 2m4f runs, though she needs to jump more cleanly than on her last outing (U).|

runners_data.name: Daphne Blake
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed — no form string, no going or distance history available, lightly raced flag attached; Peter Maher sends her a long way from base and without data this is a pure unknown that could land anywhere in the field.|

runners_data.name: Doesthatmakesense
runners_data.note: The fades-in-finish flag is a significant concern for a prominent-style horse over 2m6½f on Good ground; three runs all resulted in double-digit finishes and the form string (0P0) offers no encouragement that she can see out this longer trip.|

runners_data.name: Free A Minute
runners_data.note: Carries both a hold-up style and a fades-in-finish flag — a tough combination over 2m6½f — and three recent runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 13th, 12th, and 7th; the 21-day turnaround gives little cause for optimism here.|

runners_data.name: I Dont Really Care
runners_data.note: Ray Hackett's five-year-old has only two runs in the book, finishing 4th and 14th, with the best result coming at 2m2f on Good — the step up to 2m6½f is a significant stamina question mark for a hold-up type with limited experience.|

runners_data.name: Labondance
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins sends out this five-year-old for the first time in 286 days, which is a notable absence; all five career runs came on Heavy ground at Navan and this is a completely different surface (Good at Ballinrobe) so going suitability is a genuine unknown despite a style tag of uncertain.|

runners_data.name: Run For Power
runners_data.note: Three runs on Good ground have produced finishes of 6th, 4th, and 12th — modest form for a hold-up type over shorter trips, and the step up to 2m6½f with no evidence of stamina beyond 2m1f makes this a speculative entry; the 17-day turnaround is fine but the form doesn't inspire.|

runners_data.name: Castle Garden
runners_data.note: J J Slevin rides for Donal Hassett and this four-year-old has only one run to her name (3rd), leaving her profile wide open; the lightly-raced flag and unexposed angle make her a legitimate dark horse in a weak maiden field if the stamina trip suits.|

runners_data.name: Gunner Girl
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good ground, both resulting in double-digit finishes (13th, 7th); a four-year-old hold-up type with no evidence of staying 2m6½f and a modest early form profile — needs significant improvement to feature here.|

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' four-year-old is the confirmed pace-setter and Brian Hayes will use that role to control the race; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) flags that it may be racing slightly outside its optimal tactical comfort zone, and while its Good-ground record is adequate, it will need everything to go its way to last home over this stamina-testing trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Ronnie's Rascal is the confirmed front-runner and, with Willie Mullins' booking of Brian Hayes, will be sent to make the running from flag to flag over this 2m6½f trip on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Goodgollymissholly, Amina, Cool Native, and Doesthatmakesense are all prominent-style types who will push for position behind the leader, creating a competitive early sectional that should produce a genuinely honest gallop rather than a dawdle. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all find their natural position — Clash Gold, a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map, is most likely to end up racing slightly further back than its rivals would prefer, limiting its ability to produce a late run off a true pace. This race shape — a single, consistent front-runner setting a sustainable rhythm on Good ground over a staying trip — most favours horses with a prominent running style who can track the pace efficiently, travel into contention turning for home, and sustain their effort through the final obstacles without needing a strong late sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Ronnie's Rascal sets a genuine but sustainable gallop and the prominent trackers travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Goodgollymissholly and Amina, both proven prominent types on Good ground, will be ideally placed to challenge in the straight having raced within striking distance throughout; the honest pace over 2m6½f on a sound surface suits those with proven stamina and clean jumping.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Ronnie's Rascal goes too hard early and the field concertinas in the final mile.
scenarios.body: A collapse in the leader's stamina reserve would open the door for horses who have been restrained slightly off the pace, allowing Cool Native or Castle Garden to pick up the pieces with fresh legs; this is the scenario where Clash Gold's natural hold-up profile becomes a genuine asset rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ronnie's Rascal is allowed to control proceedings at a comfortable clip and none of the prominent types can close the gap.
scenarios.body: With a Mullins-trained hurdler on Good ground and Brian Hayes dictating every fraction, Ronnie's Rascal could simply control the race from the front and win on the bridle; this scenario is tempered by its STYLE_FIT tag suggesting it may not reproduce its best in this tactical role in a competitive field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition, Improver Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the extended 2m6½f trip and a testing honest gallop cause wholesale fatigue, leaving the race to a lightly-raced unexposed type.
scenarios.body: Daphne Blake or Castle Garden, both lightly raced and carrying unknown ceilings, could benefit if the race becomes a stamina test that exposes the limitations of more exposed rivals; this scenario is unlikely but possible given the number of horses with uninspiring recent form strings in this maiden.

watchPoints.text: Watch Goodgollymissholly and Amina at the early stages — both will push for position behind Ronnie's Rascal and if either gets a comfortable berth in second or third, they hold the clearest profile to challenge from the front rank in the straight.

Monitor Clash Gold's position jumping off — as a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map, if it gets shuffled back to its natural position at the rear it may lack the straight-line room to deliver its best finishing effort over this trip.

Ronnie's Rascal's early gallop rate is key — if Brian Hayes sends it clear and the pace becomes too strong too soon on Good ground, the prominent pack will come under pressure a long way from home and the race could be thrown wide open.

Castle Garden and Daphne Blake are both lightly-raced unknowns ridden by strong jockeys (Slevin and Shinnick) — either could outrun their experience if their unexposed stamina profile matches the 2m6½f trip.

The Doesthatmakesense and Free A Minute fade flags are worth tracking in running — both carry prominent/hold-up styles with proven tendency to stop late, and in a genuine gallop at this trip they are likely to be swallowed up in the final half-mile.

races.name: Jerry McDonnell Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Front-runner operating out of her natural lead role according to the style tag, but Emmet Mullins's yard is in decent recent form (1/5 T14) and she has consistent Good-ground placing form over similar trips — the key asset here is simply that no one will force the issue early.
runners_data.comment: Giorgia Rose has been a model of consistency, finishing third four times in her last five starts, and has experience over today's trip and conditions — the main concern is whether she can convert that reliability into a win, as she remains winless in recent starts despite carrying a hefty 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Joshua Chamberlain
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer with one win from 15 similar-going starts but a placed run over 22f on Good recently; Gerard Keane's runner carries 163lbs and the step back up in trip after a flat run at 16f is likely to suit.
runners_data.comment: Joshua Chamberlain, rated 97 and the top-rated of 19, brings a win four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, making him hard to oppose under 163 lb after 34 days off — a run to sharpen him up cannot be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Gerrys Wish
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the mount for the high-powered Gordon Elliott yard (4/37 T14) on a five-year-old who has placed four times from 12 starts on similar going — the 'b' headgear is noted and form figures of 2-2-2 over similar distances suggest a consistent stayer.
runners_data.comment: Gerrys Wish has been placed three times in her last five starts but has a pulled-up run to her name and she remains yet to win in recent starts; has run over today's going before and returns after 32 days, though 162 lb is a stiff ask ranked fifth of nineteen.

runners_data.name: The Vegas Raider
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning quickly (14 days) for the Heffernan yard; sparse recent form with a pull-up in the sequence and limited Good-going wins from 15 comparable starts make him a risky proposition despite a placed run over 22f.
runners_data.comment: The Vegas Raider has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 94 by us, ranks second of nineteen in this field — a solid threat despite carrying 160 lb, though he is yet to win in his last five starts and that blank record remains the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Ancient Myth
runners_data.note: Consistent record of finishing mid-to-back in the field (0W from 15 similar-going runs), and the form string reads 0000 — little encouragement from recent outings, though one previous win and placed runs on similar going flag a degree of ability.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last four starts, Ancient Myth is lightly raced and open to further improvement, returning after 39 days off carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Barryroe Madam
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose best similar-going form shows a placed run at 24f; the sprint finish flag is absent but her record on Good is moderate (1W from 15) and the competitive 19-runner field represents a tough assignment.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Barryroe Madam nonetheless steps back in distance and going conditions she has experience of, and her fourth last time out hints at a return to form, with our rating of 92 making her a legitimate threat — the weight burden of 159 lb is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: My Good Pal
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard is in excellent form (7/27 T14) and this prominent-style seven-year-old has multiple placed efforts on Good ground including a win at 24f — the 'tp' headgear combination and 15-day return add positives, and the trip looks ideal.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in recent starts but winless in his last five, My Good Pal brings distance and going experience to the table and a trainer firing at 26% over the past fortnight; the 159 lb burden and a ranking of tenth of nineteen temper expectations.

runners_data.name: It's Time Again
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer who has raced almost exclusively on Good going (14/15 similar-going runs) and carries 'p' headgear — the form string flags a fall and some modest finishes but the trip is familiar and consistent participation at the level is evident.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, and a fell and pulled-up among those recent outings raise clear questions about reliability, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround at 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Ballyminnion Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a stamina fade flag and a form string that reads P-0080 — no placed runs from four comparable starts and the finish-fade concern in a 19-runner field at this trip is a meaningful negative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up on one occasion, Ballyminnion Boy at least returns on a quick turnaround of 17 days with going experience in his favour, though carrying 155 lb looks a stiff ask for a gelding ranked ninth of nineteen.

runners_data.name: Ranger Billy
runners_data.note: J J Slevin provides the key upgrade for this prominent-style ten-year-old; has placed three times from 15 similar-going starts and ran third over 22f recently — the 14-day return and 'p' headgear are noted and Slevin's booking lifts interest considerably.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with two pulled-up efforts a concern, Ranger Billy does bring distance and going experience and ran third two starts back to suggest some capability, though 153 lb is no easy burden for a gelding ranked seventh of nineteen.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Soldier
runners_data.note: Returning from 1038 days off, this nine-year-old's true style is hold-up but the oversupply of closers in the field means he cannot secure that position naturally — the extended absence is the dominant concern, with just two from four comparable Good-ground runs.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win in his last five starts but that sole success came over 1,000 days ago, leaving fitness a major question mark; has run over today's trip and a rating of 85 offers some encouragement, though recent efforts since that win have been modest at best.

runners_data.name: Chanceitlucky
runners_data.note: Adrian Murray's seven-year-old is genuinely a hold-up horse whose natural finishing position is off the pace, but the weight of closers in this field means he is mapped to midfield — the 't' headgear is new and five from six Good-ground runs show course-type compatibility, yet the style compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Chanceitlucky looks up against it here, carrying 151 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, though his recent finishes offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: John McConnell's five-year-old (2/23 T14) ran just nine days ago and has two placed efforts from 15 similar-going starts including a second at 16f — his natural tendency to race held up is constrained by this field's composition, and the quick reappearance adds a note of caution.
runners_data.comment: Fine Print arrives on the back of a sixth last time out and has been winless in his last five starts, with a fourth three starts back offering some encouragement, though his 150 lb burden and a ranking of twelfth of nineteen make a reversal of fortune difficult to envisage.

runners_data.name: Phildante
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good ground and has a respectable placed record (1W, 2P from 15 similar-going starts) — a genuine hold-up operator whose best chance would be a strong pace scenario, but the style redistribution means he cannot count on running his own race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 19 on our figures, Phildante faces a stiff ask, and a fall interrupting her recent sequence does little to inspire confidence, though she won last time out and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Tawny Lea
runners_data.note: Form of 08R0 tells a difficult story, and the finish-fade tag compounds the concern; this six-year-old's true hold-up style is compromised by the size of the hold-up contingent, and 31 days off does not resolve the underlying form issues.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Tawny Lea arrives 31 days between runs and yet to score, but her recent form — including a refusal two starts back — leaves her profile hard to read and questions remain ahead of this assignment.

runners_data.name: Princess Felicia
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good ground including a second at 20f, and Peter Smithers claims 5lbs — the finish-fade flag and the fact this hold-up mare is unlikely to get her natural rear-of-field position both temper what is otherwise a modestly encouraging form profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Princess Felicia faces a stiff ask under 146 lb, though she has placed in three of those outings and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Tantrum Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old without a jockey listed in the data — the finish-fade flag applies, and while two fourth-place finishes show some level of consistency, the hold-up style is further compromised by the redistribution issue in this big field.
runners_data.comment: Tantrum Boy has been winless in his last five starts, with a pair of fourths his best efforts and three worse finishes beneath that, and a rating of 75 ranked 15th of 19 here offers little encouragement, though the 20-day break is reasonable and he has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: But What About Me
runners_data.note: Returning from 500 days off for Barry Murphy, who has just one runner in the T14 window — the extended layoff is the primary concern, and the finish-fade flag alongside a hold-up style poorly suited to this field shape makes the task very difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and off the track for 500 days, But What About Me faces a stiff task carrying 149 lb, ranked 14 of 19 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going is the one modest positive.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: 327 days off for a six-year-old whose form figures read /0900- with consistent mid-to-back finishes on Good ground — the finish-fade tag applies, the trainer has just one runner in the T14 window, and it is hard to identify a realistic route to success on this evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning after a lengthy 327-day absence, St Anthonys Corner faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 88 suggests she retains ability above her official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Giorgia Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival likely to challenge her for the lead — she should settle into a comfortable, controlled rhythm from the front over this 2m6½f trip on Good ground. The pace she generates will be honest but not frantic, creating a clean gallop that rewards horses able to travel prominently without expending excessive early energy. My Good Pal, Joshua Chamberlain, Ranger Billy and It's Time Again are the likely prominent trackers, meaning the front quarter of the field will be fairly compact and organised. This race shape — a single controlled front-runner, solid prominent cover, and a big field — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with good stamina reserves who can challenge from the home turn rather than late-finishing hold-up types who will face significant traffic and too much ground to make up. The field holds considerably more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Chanceitlucky, Fine Print, Phildante, Princess Felicia and Tawny Lea are all genuine closers repositioned into a midfield mapping, with Giorgia Rose and My Good Pal most likely to dictate and secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Giorgia Rose Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Giorgia Rose is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, sustainable gallop that saps the stamina of those tracking.
scenarios.body: Giorgia Rose uses her prominent style to lead from the front, and with no meaningful pressure, dictates pace and jumps well to keep rivals honest — prominent trackers who travel smoothly into the home turn are perfectly positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and the prominent-to-midfield movers travel fluently throughout.
scenarios.body: My Good Pal and Joshua Chamberlain track Giorgia Rose comfortably and challenge from the second-last, their class and stamina at this trip proving decisive in a finish between prominent handlers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to cause attrition at the front and a well-handicapped stayer picks through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Gerrys Wish or Phildante, both with strong form over similar distances on Good ground, travel through the pack on the bridle and hit the front at a crucial moment when the leaders begin to tie up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly hot and the front rank burns out, leaving the extreme hold-up runners with a clear passage.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given that true closers like Chanceitlucky, Tawny Lea and Fine Print are all out of their natural position in this race map and face the twin challenges of a manageable pace and significant traffic in a big field.

watchPoints.text: Giorgia Rose is uncontested in front and if Emmet Mullins's mare jumps cleanly from the off and settles into her rhythm, she could prove very difficult to peg back in this shape — watch how composed she looks at the top of the home straight.

My Good Pal's trainer Gavin Cromwell is firing on all cylinders (7/27 T14) and this horse has the style and stamina to be dangerous tracking the leader — watch whether Mr B M Coonan gets a clean position behind the pace from the first hurdle.

Jack Kennedy on Gerrys Wish for Gordon Elliott is a booking that commands attention in any race; watch whether Kennedy can position this consistent Good-ground stayer close enough to challenge from the home turn rather than being left with too much to do.

With 19 runners, the sheer volume of hold-up horses repositioned into midfield — including Chanceitlucky, Fine Print and Phildante — means traffic congestion turning for home is a significant risk; watch for crowding inside the final four hurdles that could end winning chances prematurely.

Ranger Billy's booking of J J Slevin for the Heffernan yard is a notable jockey upgrade worth monitoring — if Slevin can get this prominent ten-year-old into his natural rhythm early, the placed form over 22f on Good suggests he may be underestimated at a handicap mark of 84.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Addragoole
runners_data.note: OR 140, won over similar Good-ground conditions 24 days ago for Gavin Cromwell and Keith Donoghue; prominent racer who should slot in just behind Runcok and is the classiest horse in the field if fully forward from a recent reappearance.|
runners_data.comment: Addragoole has experience of today's distance and going, a trainer firing at 26% in the last fortnight, and a recent win in his last five starts to his name; the concern is that his latest two efforts have been modest, and 161 lb is a stern ask if he lacks peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Ma Jacks Hill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has winning form on Good over this sort of trip and Joshua Halford claims 7lbs, but being a natural prominent type who will be squeezed back into midfield by the crowd of forward runners significantly dilutes his chance in this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out and eighth two starts back, Ma Jacks Hill has been struggling for consistency, and our rating has him ranked last of six in this field; a win three starts back offers a crumb of hope, but 161 lb makes the task no easier despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Runcok
runners_data.note: The lone genuine front-runner; J J Slevin takes the mount and Good-ground form figures suggest he handles conditions, making his ability to dictate unchallenged the single most important factor in how this race is run.|
runners_data.comment: Runcok has finished sixth in each of his last two starts and ranks fifth of six on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a win in his last five starts and experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy partners this hold-up horse who is just two days since his last run — notable freshness concern — but has placed form over 2m and stays well; pure closer dependent on a stronger pace than Runcok is likely to provide.|
runners_data.comment: Bowensonfire has shown progressive consistency in recent starts, placing third last time out and second two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead; the concern is he returns just two days after his last outing, and at 156 lb the weight could prove the decisive factor.

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins and Danny Mullins, but Bunting has a limited win-strike on Good going and — crucially — is a true prominent racer who will struggle to secure that berth in this congested forward group, racing in a position that doesn't suit and with a style-fit discount to reflect that.|
runners_data.comment: Bunting has run over today's trip and going before, and his trainer is in fine fettle at 28% over the past fortnight, making him a lively threat despite carrying 156 lb; the concern is a run of consecutive disappointing finishes that leaves him yet to score in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Jazzy Matty
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 145 and the highest-class runner in the race; Cian Collins has had no runs in the last 14 days, and Jazzy Matty's prominent style should allow him to sit handy, but recent form figures (5625-6) raise questions about consistency rather than suitability to this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Jazzy Matty arrives here just two days after his last start, bringing strong recent fitness, and his second three starts back underlines he can mix it at this level, even if he has been winless in recent starts. He has run over today's trip and going, and the overall profile makes him our pick from the six runners.

races.paceDynamic: Runcok is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no genuine rival to push him along, he should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on Good ground over 2m1f at Ballinrobe. Addragoole, Jazzy Matty, Ma Jacks Hill, and Bunting all carry prominent tendencies, but the field holds more forward-going types than can realistically secure that territory — Ma Jacks Hill and Bunting are both true prominent racers who will find themselves shuffled into midfield roles they do not naturally fill, reducing their effectiveness. Bowensonfire is the only genuine hold-up horse, giving the race a compressed mid-pack shape where several horses will be racing out of their preferred positions. This race shape strongly favours Runcok if he travels well in front, and — because the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to stretch the field — it also rewards prominent types like Addragoole and Jazzy Matty who can land close to him without expending excess energy, making class and jumping fluency the decisive late factors rather than any late sprint from held-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Runcok Controls From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Runcok travels comfortably in front and the prominent horses cannot sustain a challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: Runcok sets a manageable pace unchallenged, arrives at the final fences full of running, and his Good-ground form and sole front-runner status make him near-impossible to dislodge; this shape rewards front-running class and clean jumping.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pegs Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer — most likely Addragoole or Jazzy Matty — tracks Runcok closely and outjumps or outclasses him in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Runcok's lead is sustainable but not unassailable, and a classier rival sitting a length off his girth can pounce at the second-last; Addragoole's OR of 140 and recent win form on Good gives this thread the most credibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and Bowensonfire is produced with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Bowensonfire, handled by Jack Kennedy and with placed form at this distance on Good, is the only true closer in the race and needs a strong pace to overhaul the leaders; this scenario is constrained by the likelihood of Runcok keeping things comfortable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish — Midfielders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Ma Jacks Hill or Bunting, despite racing out of their natural prominent role, find enough room to challenge in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Both horses are effectively racing out of role in the midfield they are mapped to, suppressing their chance; a messy or falsely-run race could bring them back into contention, but their redistribution flags mean this is the least bankable shape.

watchPoints.text: Runcok's jumping — if he makes an error at a key fence in front, Addragoole or Jazzy Matty are positioned to capitalise immediately given how close they will be tracking him.
Bowensonfire ran just two days ago; monitor market moves and any jockey/trainer comments, as a horse this fresh to back-to-back runs may not be at peak sharpness for a chasing effort.

Ma Jacks Hill and Bunting — both natural prominent types — may jostle for position in the early stages as they attempt to recover their preferred spot, risking interference or wasted energy in the first half-mile.

The Good-ground going report is consistent across all races at Ballinrobe today, so no runner faces a going surprise, but Jazzy Matty's sim-going record of 11/15 runs on this surface is the strongest in the field and worth noting if the race is truly run to suit prominent types.

races.name: Corrib Oil Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's hold-up horse carries solid good-ground form (2W8P in similar conditions) and his recent run string of 3-2-3 at long distances marks him as a consistent stayer who should travel comfortably off Slurricane's pace; the 24-day break looks straightforward and this trip on good ground suits him well.
runners_data.comment: Donnie Devito has been a model of consistency, finishing third three times and second once in his last five starts, and has experience of today's distance and going — the chief concern is that seventh last time out suggests he may need to bounce back sharply carrying 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' charge has shown ability in good-ground conditions but his good-ground sample in similar races shows only 0W1P from six runs, and his natural front-running instincts will be suppressed by the field's make-up — he is unlikely to secure his preferred prominent berth and faces a harder task operating from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Fou De Toi also carries a hefty 166 lb, making him hard to fancy despite having experience of today's distance and going and a trainer firing at 28% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins' seven-year-old is consistent on good ground with a 3/6 similar-going record and a recent second and third suggesting he is in fair form; he is one of the prominent types most likely to actually get his natural position behind Slurricane, and clean jumping over this extended trip will be key.
runners_data.comment: Jeroboam Machin has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 166 lb is the chief concern for a gelding yet to win in his last four outings.

runners_data.name: Kevin's Pride
runners_data.note: John McConnell's horse is a genuine front-runner whose natural aggression for prominent positioning will be difficult to execute in this field with Slurricane in front and other prominent types competing for the same ground; a 45-day absence adds mild fitness query, and his best form (2W3P similar going) came when able to race closer to his preferred role.
runners_data.comment: Kevin's Pride won four starts back but has finished fourth, fifth, and fourth in his three most recent outings, suggesting he's finding rivals tough to pass of late; the 45-day break and experience over today's trip and going give him a fighting chance at a rating of 115.

runners_data.name: Maverick Mack
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old won on heavy ground at Fairyhouse but his recent form string includes a fall, a brought-pulled-up, and a blank — jumping reliability is the central concern over 2m7½f of chasing; if he has schooled well since, he arrives with natural hold-up ability and good-ground handler status, but the 78-day break and that form profile demand caution.
runners_data.comment: Maverick Mack has endured a wretched recent sequence — pulled up, brought down, and unseated in his last three starts — and ranked eighth of nine on our figures he faces a stiff task, though going experience and a win two starts earlier offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's eight-year-old has a decent placed record (0W3P in similar going) and races prominently, but a 3/22f and 2/20f placing on good ground suggests he handles the conditions; at age eight in a beginners' chase he carries more experience than most, though his record of consistent minor placings rather than winning suggests he needs things to go right.
runners_data.comment: Mickie Angel has been in fine fettle of late, placing third last time out and third two starts back, with a second three starts back bolstering a consistent profile; he carries 166 lb on ground and over a trip he has experience of, and at 16 days fresh, conditions look ideal despite being yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rusty Harkness
runners_data.note: Henry de Bromhead's six-year-old arrives with the most persuasive recent form in the race — a win and a second in his last two starts including a victory over 24 furlongs on good ground — and Darragh O'Keeffe is a booking that commands respect; a prominent racing style that is genuine and likely to be accommodated makes him a key player in most scenarios.
runners_data.comment: Rusty Harkness has experience of today's trip and going, and his recent form includes a win last time out plus a couple of placed efforts, but a rating of 112 leaves him ranked seventh of nine and he faces a stiff task at this weight of 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Slurricane
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's five-year-old is the confirmed lone front-runner but his own form figures are alarming — a recent string of 0, 9th, 10th, 8th, 14th — and while he will dictate terms, his ability to sustain that advantage to the line over 2m7½f on good ground is highly questionable given that profile; the [STYLE_FIT] flag reflects that his overall chance is materially discounted despite controlling the shape.
runners_data.comment: Slurricane arrives on the back of going experience and a solid rating of 119 that ranks him third among the nine runners, making him a genuine threat despite being winless in his last five starts; the main concern is a heavy weight of 166 lb.

runners_data.name: Jolie Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's mare races as a hold-up type with a strong sample of good-ground form (14/15 runs on similar ground) and the hg:h headgear flag is noted; a 27-day break looks fine, but a recent string including a 15th and a 6th adds caution, and Phillip Enright will need her jumping to be sharp over this marathon trip if she is to convert her hold-up profile into a finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Jolie Jewel at least shows some placed form, with a second two starts back and a third three starts back, and she has experience of today's distance and going; the 159 lb burden, however, is a stiff ask if she is to reverse that recent slide.

races.paceDynamic: Slurricane is the confirmed front-runner and will set sail from the front in what is a 2m7½f beginners' chase on good ground at Ballinrobe — a trip and surface that rewards a measured, economical gallop rather than a tearaway pace. With Slurricane largely uncontested up front, the tempo is expected to be sustainable and controlled, meaning the race will unfold as a genuine test of jumping accuracy and staying stamina rather than a speed-driven affair. This field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Fou De Toi and Kevin's Pride are genuine front-runners remapped to midfield on the shape chart, with Jeroboam Machin and Rusty Harkness the prominent horses most likely to actually slot in behind Slurricane. The tactical verdict is clear — with a lone front-runner dictating a true but unforced gallop, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine stayers who travel kindly and finish well, particularly those with demonstrated form on good ground at extended distances.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slurricane Controls, Stayers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Slurricane bowls along at a fair clip unchallenged and the race develops into a searching test of stamina in the final mile.
scenarios.body: Slurricane sets an uncontested pace that suits those travelling efficiently off it, leaving the race to be decided between hold-up horses and genuine prominent types who can close strongly over the last few fences; the extended 2m7½f on good ground rewards horses who conserve energy through the race. Hold-up types Donnie Devito and Jolie Jewel, with demonstrated form at this sort of trip on good ground, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate Home Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin or Rusty Harkness jump well throughout and are able to press Slurricane into the home turn, forcing a decisive move before the last.
scenarios.body: A sharper middle section of the race compresses the field and rewards horses that have been travelling comfortably in the prominent positions throughout rather than having to make up ground late; good jumping becomes the decisive variable over the final three fences. Rusty Harkness, with recent winning form at this sort of trip on good ground, and Jeroboam Machin, consistent in good-ground conditions, are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Maverick Mack Powers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and hold-up horses find a clear run to deliver their challenge from off the pace in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Maverick Mack, trained by Gordon Elliott and held up off a moderate gallop, could arrive late if the front-runners stop in front of him; however, his recent form string includes a fall and a pulled-up, introducing significant uncertainty around his current jumping reliability. The scenario is possible but depends on better jumping from Maverick Mack than his recent outings suggest and a genuine collapse in pace from Slurricane.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Fou De Toi or Kevin's Pride push forward aggressively and succeed in taking their natural prominent position, injecting more pressure into the early pace than anticipated.
scenarios.body: A more truly-run gallop than the single front-runner map suggests would stretch the field earlier and potentially leave Slurricane vulnerable, favouring horses that have the class to sustain a higher cruising speed; both Fou De Toi and Kevin's Pride carry [STYLE_FIT] flags indicating they are racing out of their preferred role in the projected shape, making this scenario inherently less probable. Rusty Harkness and Jeroboam Machin, capable of racing prominently at a proper gallop, would be the main beneficiaries if the pace truly heats up.

watchPoints.text: Slurricane's form figures (0-9-10-8-14) are deeply concerning for a horse set to lead throughout — watch whether he retains any enthusiasm jumping and whether he starts to be reeled in from three out, triggering a chaotic reshuffle in the home straight.

Maverick Mack's jumping record (fall, pulled-up in recent runs) is a live risk around Ballinrobe's fences over 2m7½f — any jumping error from him could cause interference for hold-up horses travelling behind him.

Fou De Toi and Kevin's Pride are genuine prominent types who may attempt to push forward at the start despite the map placing them in midfield — if either succeeds, the early gallop could be sharper than anticipated and alter the entire race shape.

Rusty Harkness (Darragh O'Keeffe, de Bromhead) arrives in the best verifiable form in the field with a win and a second in his last two; watch how he travels in the prominent group as an indicator of whether Slurricane's pace is genuinely sustainable or not.

Donnie Devito's trainer Ross O'Sullivan also saddles Slurricane — watch for any team tactics and whether Gilligan on Donnie Devito is instructed to track Slurricane closely, which could give the hold-up horse a significant positional advantage in the straight.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Flat Race

runners_data.name: Ailbhes Gift
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Ailbhes Gift is yet to win in her last two starts, which include a fall, but with 252 days between runs she returns a lightly raced filly with plenty still to prove.

runners_data.name: Elegantemente
runners_data.comment: Elegantemente is unraced and therefore completely unexposed, with her debut here offering no form to go on but every reason to think improvement is well within reach under a big weight of 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Hee Hiles
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Hee Hiles is yet to score but arrives with a clean slate and everything to play for, carrying 159 lb as she takes her first steps in public.

runners_data.name: Indoor Sport
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Indoor Sport was fifth last time out and returns after a 45-day break; lightly raced and yet to win, she remains one to watch as she fills out her profile carrying 159 lb.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts and absent for 118 days, Mastertown Miss faces a stiff task from a rating of 72 in a 12-runner field, and 159 lb is a hefty burden; a second two starts back offers a slim crumb of comfort, but the layoff and eighth last time out make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Queens Counsel
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Queens Counsel arrives unraced and carrying 159 lb, leaving her profile entirely open to interpretation; lightly raced prospects like her can spring a surprise first time out, and there is plenty of improvement potentially to come.

runners_data.name: Rathnaleen Aj
runners_data.comment: Rathnaleen Aj has run over today's trip and going and returns on a quick turnaround of just 17 days, giving her supporters plenty to work with — though she was sixth last time out and remains yet to score, which is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: River Moy
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last two starts and ranked fifth of twelve on our figures, River Moy faces a stiff task here, though she has experience of today's going and returns on a reasonable 18-day break.

runners_data.name: She Means Business
runners_data.comment: She Means Business has run over today's trip and returns fit enough on a 20-day turnaround, with our rating of 83 placing her third among these 12, making her a live danger — though she is yet to score in recent starts, and 159 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: She Was The One
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts but consistently threatening, She Was The One brings strong recent placed form to the table — third last time out and a runner-up two starts back — with experience over today's trip and going adding confidence; the 159 lb burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: The Lodge Lane
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and lightly raced, The Lodge Lane brings solid recent form into this, having run over today's trip and going before; our rating of 110 tops the field of twelve, and 16 days between runs leaves her fresh enough to go close.

runners_data.name: Zara's Dream
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Zara's Dream arrives with plenty left to discover, and a trainer firing at 28% over the past fortnight gives connections every reason for quiet confidence as she steps into the spotlight carrying 159 lb.
